title: Careful, Guinevere
dateline: The first morning of the watch.
mood: One ordinary morning, one week of watch duty, and a corridor of tall windows where everything changes.

hero.alt: Comic panel in a dim corridor: pink-haired Guinevere leaps with her fist thrown at a clawed Ender while black-haired Vexana, back to back with her, fires a bolt of light from her staff into another.
hero.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana comic, page 9

segs.t: Guinevere came out of her room at first light with her ponytail still in her fist. Vexana was waiting in the corridor in her running things.
“I’ve decided,” said Guinevere, tying it off. “I’m going to name every Ender in the Investigation Room.”
“They’re dead.”
“Then they won’t mind.”
Vexana caught the left bow between two fingers and tugged it level. Guinevere held still for it. It was the only time of day she held still.
They ran. Past the fountain, under the courtyard billboard, two girls back to back with GUINEVERE and VEXANA in letters taller than a person. Guinevere saluted it.
“Morning, legends.”
“You do that every day,” said Vexana.
“Someone has to.”
At the end of the run they passed the board outside the Combat office. The watch sheet was still up: INVESTIGATION ROOM WATCH. Under it stood their two names, in the same square type as a roster.
Guinevere pressed a finger to hers. “In print.”
“It’s a watch sheet.”
“In print, Vexana.”
Back in the girls’ wing they split at their doors to change for class.
“Tonight, the hall,” said Guinevere. “I’m doing the whole month’s plan twice.”
“Then I’ll call.”
“You always call.”
“Then I’ll call,” said Vexana, and went into her room.
Guinevere was knotting her tie at the mirror when the alarm went.
It was the Academy’s own alarm, three hard notes, then a voice from the speaker over her door. “Breach at the dome’s seaward foot. Enders in the Investigation Room wing. Watch pair, respond.”
That’s us.
She was out of the door with her tie half done.

Down the corridor Vexana’s door flew open. Vexana came out at a run in her uniform, tie knotted, staff in hand. The little pink-haired keychain was clipped at her belt. She pulled the door shut behind her without looking. She always shut doors.
“Heroic after all!” Guinevere shouted.
“Run,” said Vexana.
The Academy Investigation Room Corridor.
Bang, bang, bang.
Vexana fired three times down the corridor before they were through the doors. Three Enders went over.

It was a long pale corridor with tall windows down one side. Morning light fell through them in bars across the floor. Two windows were smashed in. The sea wind blew through them, and with it the city’s sirens.
Through the glass, down by the water below the Academy’s wall, the dome’s foot was torn. Gray shapes were still climbing in through the gap.

The corridor was full of them. Tall Enders on long legs, with claws as long as an arm. A crate from the Science Division lay split open, its old plates spilled across the floor. One Ender was dragging a dead Ender’s arm toward a broken window.
Her drones snapped up at her shoulders. Guinevere went in with her fists. Vexana’s back came against hers. They worked down the corridor like that.
An Ender swung at her. Its chest split, and the core glowed in the gap. Her fist went in.
“Nine!”
“Ten,” said Vexana. Her bolt went over Guinevere’s shoulder into another open chest.
“That one was mine!”
“Then be faster.”
Guinevere grinned and was faster. She sprang ahead to the next one, three long strides from Vexana’s back, toward the windows.

blocks.caption: Three long strides ahead, toward the windows.

media.alt: Comic panel: Guinevere springs forward through the window light, fists ready, toward a tall gray Ender with a yellow eye.
media.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana comic, page 11

segs.t: A claw came swinging for her open side.
“I’ll end it here!” Vexana’s voice, behind her.
The bolt cracked past Guinevere’s ribs. The Ender at her side folded. She had not turned her head.
The window light was in her face. Her shadow lay behind her on the white inner wall.
All at once it was flung forward, long across the floor ahead of her, edged in purple. Some new light had come on at her back. A second shadow rose over hers. Its claw was raised.
There was no sound at all.
Her breath stopped. She was mid-swing at the Ender in front of her, and there was no time to turn.
Vexana is there.
“Careful, Guinevere!”
Vexana’s white glove struck her shoulder, hard.
Her feet left the floor. The stone came up. She hit it and rolled, glass grating under her. Her drones tumbled after her.
She came up on her knees and turned.
Behind the place where she had stood, the wall was open. A door had torn in the white, no wider than a person, its edges burning purple, black inside. A long gray leg stood out of it.
Above the leg, a claw of long blades was closed on Vexana’s hand. The hand that had pushed her.
Vexana’s boots slid on the pale floor, toward the dark.
Guinevere was on her feet before she knew it.
“No! Vexana!”
The blades had closed on her hand instead. Vexana felt them through the glove, cold.
The claw pulled. She drove the butt of her staff at the floor, and it skated on the pale stone. Her heels slid. At her back the dark waited, with no end to it.
Across the floor Guinevere was up and coming, her black-gloved hand stretched out.
The claw had come out of the wall for that open back, and it had missed.
It’s all right,
thought Vexana.
As long as she’s safe.
Her eyes ran over. She had no hand free to wipe them.
Guinevere was nearly there.
“Stay back!”
It came out of her loud enough to fill the corridor.
The cold closed over her shoulders. Guinevere’s hand came on, reaching for hers.
Stay back.
Guinevere did not stay back. She threw herself at the door with her arm out.
Her fingers closed on air, a hand short. She kept her arm out.
Then be faster.

Vexana’s face was already going. The door was closing around her. It had her to the shoulders, then to the chin. Her violet eyes stayed on Guinevere. Tears had run down to the small mole by her mouth.
Slowly the dark took the rest. For a moment a small gold point still showed in it, where her collar had been.
The door shrank to a crack in the white wall. Then there was only the wall.

blocks.caption: The dark took her, and then there was only the wall.

media.alt: Motion comic: black-haired Vexana is dragged backward into the dark, one hand reaching out; then her tearful face sinks into the closing dark, and only a thin black crack is left on the pale wall.
media.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana motion comic

segs.t: Two Enders were still in the corridor. Afterward she could not remember breaking them. When she looked again they lay in pieces under the windows, and her knuckles hurt.
The corridor went quiet.
The sea wind came in through the broken glass. Out over the city the sirens were still going. The light lay across the floor in the same bars as before.
Her drones hung at her shoulders, rings bright, waiting for something to hit.
“Vexana!”
The name rang to the far doors and came back to her. Nobody answered.
She looked for something. The staff. A glove. There was nothing. On the pale floor two black scuffs ran from where Vexana had stood to the foot of the wall. There they stopped.
The wall was white and whole.
“Open,” she told it.
It stayed white.
She knelt and laid her palm flat where the scuffs ended. The stone was cold under her glove. Her tie still hung half knotted at her throat.
In case,
Vexana had said on the roof, and folded the page smaller. Guinevere had asked in case of what. Vexana had only said it again. Then a siren went, and Guinevere never asked a third time.
Behind her, glass ticked across the stone in the wind. She turned and looked back over her shoulder.
She had never needed to before. Nobody was there.
Gold light lay across the back of her hand. She looked down.
At her collar the star was still lit.
She stared at it. It lit only when they were in sync. It took two.
Then she’s there,
thought Guinevere.
Just not here.
She laid two fingers on the star. It was warm.
She meant to say it the way she said everything, loud enough for the whole Academy.
“The Aspirant light will never go out,” she whispered.
She did not get up.
Under her two fingers, the small gold star stayed lit.
